lesson.menu_title: Who Is Rosa? — The First Regional Call
lesson.menu_desc: Introducing yourself to the new South America team, in the year the company reorganized -- 36 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 1 -- Who Is Rosa? The First Regional Call
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Rosa M. Mitiko Shida | Lesson 1 -- Who Is Rosa?
lesson.grammar_point: present simple and present continuous for professional identity

listenings.text: Rosa, hi, it is Paulo from the regional program office. I am calling about the kick-off call on Thursday. It moved from ten to eleven in the morning, Sao Paulo time, because the Santiago team asked for it. The call runs for fifty minutes and there are eleven of us on it, and it is all in English. You do not need to prepare a presentation. What we do need from every account manager is one minute at the start: your name, your city, and what your portfolio looks like today. That is it. I am sending the invitation this afternoon. Call me back if Thursday does not work for you.

Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the first commercial update of the new structure. Let me start with what is changing and what is not. The commercial teams in Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Colombia now report into one regional office instead of four separate ones. That is the change. What is not changing is your client portfolio. Nobody is moving accounts this quarter. The second point is meetings. From September, we run one regional call a week, on Thursday mornings, and it replaces the four local calls you have today. And the third point, which matters most for the people in this room: the working language of the regional office is English. Not because anybody prefers it, but because eleven people from four countries need one language to share a call.

items.situation: The regional call starts and the director says: 'Rosa, would you introduce yourself to the group?' You have sixty seconds.
tips: Start with role, then city, then portfolio
One sentence each -- finish every sentence you start

items.situation: A colleague from Santiago asks: 'Are the accounts moving to the regional office?'
tips: Say what is not changing first
Nobody is moving accounts this quarter

items.situation: Somebody speaks fast and you lose the last sentence completely.
tips: Could you say that again, a little more slowly?

items.situation: Diego asks: 'What is the hardest part of your week?'
tips: Use workload or keep up with
Two short sentences, then ask him the same question

items.situation: The director asks: 'Anything you need from the regional office?'
tips: A short request is better than a long explanation
It would help if the client list came in English too

items.situation: A new colleague asks: 'How long have you been with the company?'
tips: Give the number, then one detail about the role
Add where you were before -- tourism, then aviation

extra_audio.text: Diego introduces himself and explains that he is calling from the Bogota office. Rosa gives her name and says she is in charge of the corporate clients in Sao Paulo. Diego asks how big her client portfolio is, and Rosa answers with the number and the kind of company. Rosa explains that the commercial area is rolling out the new regional structure this year. Diego asks whether she is coming to the convention, and Rosa says she is, and asks him the same question back.
